---
title: "Symmetric INT8 Quantization"
date: 2026-08-17
categories: [Quantization, PyTorch]
---

## Idea

For symmetric INT8 quantization, we map floating-point values to an integer range
using a scale factor.

For a weight tensor \(W\), define

$$
s = \frac{\max |W|}{127}.
$$

The quantized value is

$$
q = \operatorname{round}\left(\frac{W}{s}\right),
$$

with

$$
q \in [-127,127].
$$

The approximate dequantized value is

$$
\hat W = s q.
$$

## PyTorch example

```{python}
import torch

weights = torch.tensor([-1.2, -0.2, 0.4, 1.0])

scale = weights.abs().max() / 127
q = torch.round(weights / scale).clamp(-127, 127).to(torch.int8)

print("scale:", scale)
print("quantized:", q)
print("dequantized:", q.float() * scale)
```

## Per-channel quantization

For a matrix

$$
W \in \mathbb{R}^{C_{out} \times C_{in}},
$$

we can compute a separate scale for each output channel:

```{python}
weights = torch.randn(4, 16)

abs_max = weights.abs().max(dim=-1).values
scales = abs_max / 127

q = torch.round(weights / scales[:, None])
q = q.clamp(-127, 127).to(torch.int8)

q.shape, scales.shape
```

## Things worth remembering

- Symmetric quantization usually uses zero-point \(z=0\).
- Per-channel quantization generally reduces error compared with one scale for the whole tensor.
- `127`, rather than `128`, is commonly used when keeping the range symmetric around zero.
